title: Due Diligence on Carbon Credits Issued by Gold Standard and Verra
what_it_is: Due Diligence on Carbon Credits Issued by Gold Standard and Verra

sections.label: Carbon credit MOUs and criteria
sections.summary: MOUs with Gold Standard and Verra are not legally binding, and Singapore will publish a whitelist of acceptable international carbon credits later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The MOUs are not legally binding and do not qualify all ICC issued by Gold Standard and Verra, as companies must meet the environmental integrity criteria of the Singapore Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Gold Standard and Verra were selected as MOU partners as they are two of the largest carbon crediting programmes which have been accepted by the International Civil Aviation Organisation or ICAO to issue carbon credits for compliance under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation, or CORSIA for short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government is aware of The Guardian's report on rainforest credits issued by Verra and the response and clarification issued by Verra.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We take all scrutiny of carbon markets and projects seriously, and are committed to ensuring that carbon credits uphold high environmental integrity standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will take these developments into account as we finalise the environmental integrity criteria for the ICC that are eligible for carbon tax offset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will publish a whitelist of acceptable ICC later this year, which will include eligible host countries, carbon crediting programmes and methodologies.

sections.label: Considering developments in carbon markets
sections.summary: Singapore will consider developments in standard settings and multilateral fora and work with stakeholders to help carbon credit offset markets develop healthily.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my main reply that we would consider all developments in standard settings or discussions or multilateral fora including in CORSIA and other discussion fora.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And we will do our best to work with stakeholders to ensure that the carbon credit offsets have a good chance of developing into a healthy set of markets.
